exposure: healthcare worker knowledge of breastfeeding guidelines
healthcare worker support practices for breastfeeding
healthcare worker profession (paediatrician, obstetrician, general practitioner, midwife)
healthcare worker confidence in providing breastfeeding advice
outcome: healthcare worker knowledge of exclusive breastfeeding definition
healthcare worker recommendation for exclusive breastfeeding duration
healthcare worker beliefs on breastfeeding contraindications for HIV-infected mothers
healthcare worker confidence in providing breastfeeding advice
healthcare worker completion of WHO Lactation Management Training
healthcare worker perceived sufficiency of prior breastfeeding training
cohort: The study cohort consisted of paediatricians, obstetricians, general practitioners, and midwives working in the Motheo district, Free State province, South Africa.
finding: The study found significant disparities and deficiencies in breastfeeding knowledge, attitudes, and support practices among different healthcare worker professions, with many showing insufficient training and adherence to current guidelines, particularly regarding exclusive breastfeeding duration and recommendations for HIV-infected mothers.
cross-section timing: The study assessed healthcare workers' knowledge, attitudes, and practices at a single point in time.
